title: The Chamber Where Stone Remembers Its Own Song

features.name: the bedrock processor
features.desc-on-touch: A massive circuit board carved into stone itself, each trace glowing faintly. You can feel vibrations through the floor — the stone is computing something at geological speed. The song it's remembering is the rhythm of its own crystalline formation.

features.name: the settling frequency
features.desc-on-touch: A smaller chip that broadcasts a tone so low you feel it in your bones. The frequency is the rate at which this stone settled, layer by layer — its autobiography rendered as sound.

features.name: the conductor of deep time
features.desc-on-touch: A wireframe hand reaches from the stone, its fingers tracing patterns in the air. It conducts the song that the entire chamber is singing — a melody that spans millennia, one note per thousand years.

features.name: the memory etched in quartz
features.desc-on-touch: Seams of quartz running through the circuit board, each one a stored note. You trace them and hear fragments — the stone remembering its own becoming, layers falling, pressure building, crystalline thought forming at the speed of tectonic patience.

inscription: the stone learned to sing at the speed it had time to remember
